Asha / team — reviewed the traffic CSV. Quick observations and an initial sizing sketch:

- Traffic shape: sustained baseline ~60 qps with daily peaks up to ~420 qps and very short tail spikes. Median sequence len ~380 tokens; 95th ~820 tokens.
- Kernel/latency impact: long sequences push memory pressure; recommend starting with 4x A100-80GB equiv nodes (reserved) + 8x burst-capacity V100/RTX-class instances for headroom.
- Autoscale policy suggestion (proposal):
  * Baseline: keep 4 reserved nodes to honor latency SLO (p50 < 80ms, p95 < 250ms).
  * Reactive scale: add 2 burst nodes for sustained >120 qps for 2 minutes; add additional increments of 2 nodes up to 8 burst nodes.
  * Pre-warm rule: when predicted ramp (based on prefix cache hit delta) > 150 qps expected within 5 minutes, pre-warm 2 nodes.
  * Cooldown: 6 minutes for node removal to avoid flapping.

- KV/prefix caching: significant win here — if you can identify heavy prompt families we can reduce effective qps by ~20-30%. Discuss in kickoff.

Action items I propose before the kickoff:
1) Gamma to share top-20 prompt families or sample traces (if available).
2) Redwood to prepare region capacity matrix (I will take this + Logan).
3) Draft SOW skeleton for CS/ops tasks (Ben to produce).

I'll attach the preliminary region-capacity-matrix after a quick netops check.

Regards,
Monica Patel
Implementation Lead, Customer Success — Redwood Inference
